subject: merging core/daemon-lifecycle-resilience-20260912 into main

main_unique_commit.subject: core: keep TaskPool and evening sandbox clock if lifecycle init fails (#8)

why_not: The one commit main has that this branch does not edits ace_daemon.py - the file the sole running daemon (pid 26508) executes. That branch has since been rewritten 225 commits' worth, so merging is a real three-way merge on the hottest file in the system, not a fast-forward.

A merge would put a conflict or a regression into the daemon's code path while it is live. The repository's own rules require RED reproduction, a minimal owned fix, GREEN regression and natural daemon evidence before such a change; a merge is none of those.

No test in the suite exercises main's specific fix independently - the behaviour it protects (surviving a lifecycle init failure) is only observable when that failure happens, so 'the merge did not break it' cannot be established by running the suite.
Nothing is at risk from not merging: the branch is fully pushed and the remote is verified identical to local. The 217-commit gap is a mainline currency problem, not a data-loss one.
what_is_safe_today: Nothing further is needed for durability. refs/heads/core/daemon-lifecycle-resilience-20260912 on the remote is byte-identical to local HEAD.
how_to_do_it_safely_later: Stop the sole daemon through ACE_Daemon_Boot (never start a second one).
Merge on a branch, not on main: git checkout -b main-integration <sha> and git merge main there.
Resolve ace_daemon.py by hand against the current file; do not accept either side wholesale.
Run the full suite, then start the daemon and confirm the lifecycle-init-failure path by forcing that failure in a scratch tree, not in production.
Only after the daemon runs clean on the merged tree, merge that into main and push.
